author: Vincent Chow
description:
Prominent US lawmakers have requested information from food delivery giant DoorDash on its use of Chinese artificial intelligence models after its co-founder disclosed that they had experimented with a model from Chinese start-up Moonshot AI, developer of the Kimi models.
The move underscores growing tensions between US lawmakers and industry, as Chinese AI models have become increasingly popular among US companies looking to save costs of AI adoption.
House Select Committee on China chairman...
title: US lawmakers investigate DoorDash’s use of Moonshot AI’s Kimi K2.6 model

author: Khushboo Razdan,William Zheng
description:
US Senator Steve Daines is expected to return to China for another round of talks ahead of President Xi Jinping’s planned September visit to Washington, according to people familiar with the preparations.
The trip was intended to help finalise the agenda for what both sides hoped would be a high-stakes summit between Xi and US President Donald Trump, one of the sources said.
Daines, a Montana Republican, has emerged as an important backchannel figure between Washington and Beijing. He visited...
title: Trump envoy Steve Daines to return to Beijing as US and China lock in Xi summit agenda

author: Andrew Sheng
description:
Who will win the next war? That is the question posed on the cover of the latest Foreign Affairs magazine which explores, among other things, the US-China military and technological rivalry. At its core is a clash of strategic philosophies between the US-led order and China’s world view, which has propelled the latter’s rise to the world’s second great power.
The magazine’s contributors reflect a deeply ingrained Western strategic tradition, rooted in liberal realism, that says that the United...
title: Will US or China win the next war? That’s the wrong question to ask

author: Igor Patrick
description:
Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast received China’s ambassador to Santiago, Niu Qingbao, at the La Moneda Palace on Friday morning, in an encounter that lasted more than an hour and marked the first meeting between the two men since the right-wing leader took office in March.
According to the presidency, Kast, Foreign Minister Francisco Perez Mackenna and Foreign Affairs Undersecretary Patricio Torres used the meeting to review their bilateral agenda, the minister’s coming trip to China and the...
title: Chile’s Kast courts China day after US hits exports with forced labour tariff

author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
The White House on Friday added 43 Chinese companies to a blacklist that is meant to block imports made with alleged forced labour in Xinjiang, marking the third time this week Washington has announced measures aimed at China.
Enforcing the Uygur Forced Labour Prevention Act (UFLPA), the Department of Homeland Security increased its entity list by 30 per cent to include companies in sectors ranging from food and cotton to pharmaceuticals, metals and lithium production.
The UFLPA was passed by...
title: US adds 43 Chinese companies to Uygur forced labour blacklist

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
The US-China tech rivalry has escalated into a deeper battle over undersea fibre-optic cables powering the global AI boom.
As demand for cross-border data to power and train advanced systems intensifies, so does the high-stakes battle to control critical network ecosystems – mainly submarine cables that send nearly 99 per cent of intercontinental data traffic at immense speed.
Beijing on Tuesday accused Washington of “politicising” global undersea cable networks, following reports that the US...
title: How global AI boom is intensifying US-China undersea stand-off

author: Finbarr Bermingham
description:
The European Union’s foreign affairs chief, Kaja Kallas, is expected to travel to China in the autumn for her first face-to-face meeting with Foreign Minister Wang Yi since a bruising encounter in Brussels last summer, according to multiple people familiar with the planning.
It would also mark Kallas’ first trip to Beijing since taking on her role in 2024.
The trip – with a date yet to be confirmed – would revolve around the bilateral “strategic dialogue”, a mostly annual format in which the...
title: Top EU diplomat Kallas expected to visit Beijing in autumn amid deepest strains in years

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Under new regulations, the Chinese government will soon be able to ban citizens from leaving the country if they violate export controls or rules on technology transfers.
The measures were announced by the State Council, China’s cabinet, on Friday and are set to take effect on September 15.
The Ministry of Commerce and other departments can enforce exit bans on citizens if their breaches “endanger national industrial or technological security”, according to the State Council.
The regulations...
title: Beijing to impose exit bans for export control, tech transfer breaches

author: Chao Kong
description:
In June 1958, as China’s Great Leap Forward campaign gained traction, state media began reporting astronomical agricultural yields, including claims from central Henan province of over 3,000 jin per mu – more than 22 tonnes per hectare.
That month, scientist Qian Xuesen, father of China’s rocket programme, published theoretical calculations on maximum solar energy conversion during crop photosynthesis, which political cadres cited to validate the claims.
In the following months, reported yield...
title: China is making a great leap forward in food production – this time for real

author: Liu Zhen
description:
China has given a rare acknowledgement that it has built more nuclear missile silos in recent years, with state television airing a documentary on the construction programme.
In an interview with state broadcaster CCTV, Cui Daohu, an officer with a PLA Rocket Force engineering unit, described his contribution to building the missile positions that he called China’s “strategic trump cards”, saying the schedule was tight but had been completed on time.
“We build homes for missiles. Each position...
title: China signals buildout of nuclear missile silos for ‘strategic trump cards’

author: Victoria Bela
description:
British publication The Economist has come under fire across social media for calling China an “eco-authoritarian” state over its Yangtze River fishing ban, with some users calling out the outlet for its use of the “but at what cost” trope.
In a piece published on July 27, the publication outlined China’s efforts to restore Asia’s longest waterway, which has experienced decades of environmental degradation, leading to a decline in fish and other species populations.
“The Chinese Communist Party,...
title: But at what cost? The Economist draws backlash over ‘eco-authoritarian’ China label

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Japanese F-35A stealth fighters are flying training missions over Australia for the first time in Exercise Pitch Black – part of a broader defence pivot that experts say could bolster US and allied resilience against Beijing in a Taiwan contingency.
The multinational exercise, held every two years and featuring around 100 aircraft, runs from July 20 to August 7. It comes just days after Japanese, US and Australian F-35s trained together during the inaugural Southern Cross drills.
Southern Cross...
title: Why Japanese stealth fighters over Australia signal a strategic pivot against China

author: Finbarr Bermingham
description:
Last Thursday, the European Union added 14 Chinese companies to its latest round of sanctions, accusing them of providing support for Russia’s war against Ukraine – but few of the names were recognisable to anyone outside narrow trading and compliance circles.
Officials were taken aback less than 24 hours later, when Beijing – which had been notified of the ragtag group of traders and freight forwarders to be listed by the EU as far back as June – fired back ferociously. Unlike the long notice...
title: EU-China trade war: Beijing turns the screws as Brussels tests limits of restraint

author: Raymond Ma,Neil Denslow
description:
China’s factory activity unexpectedly slipped into contraction for the first time in five months, and construction activity fell to its lowest since the pandemic, underscoring a divide in the nation’s economy that complicates efforts to revive growth.
The official manufacturing purchasing managers’ index (PMI) dropped to 49.2 in July, missing the 50.1 median estimate in a Bloomberg poll of economists. Construction and services, part of non-manufacturing PMI, tumbled to 49 from 50.2 a month...
title: China factories cool, CXMT surges, PLA marks anniversary

author: Junjie Wang
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping held discussions with the leaders of Slovakia and Namibia in Beijing during July, as well as meeting the heads of Cambodia, Thailand and Kazakhstan in Shanghai on the sidelines of the World AI Conference.
Xi also hosted North Korean Premier Pak Thae‑song in Beijing following his state visit and meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un in June.
So far this year, Xi has met with 26 national leaders, including US President Donald Trump. There may be three more...
title: Xi Jinping meets foreign leaders: tracker, July 2026

author: SCMP Plus
description: This report was translated from Chinese into English using Alibaba’s Qwen3.7-Plus, then checked and tweaked for accuracy by a South China Morning Post journalist. It is for reference only, and is not the official English version of the original Chinese document. Alibaba owns the SCMP.
title: July Politburo meeting read-out

author: Amber Wang
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has called on the People’s Liberation Army to enhance its use of AI as part of a drive to develop an intelligent military.
He told a Politburo group study session that the PLA should “strengthen the military application of unmanned intelligent technologies, deepen the development and application of network information systems, and gradually build an intelligent military system,” according to state news agency Xinhua.
Xi was speaking ahead of the PLA’s 99th...
title: Xi Jinping urges Chinese armed forces to ‘strengthen military application’ of AI

author: SCMP
description:
We have selected seven stories from this week’s news across Hong Kong, mainland China, the wider Asia region and beyond that resonated with our readers and shed light on topical issues. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. Chinese satellite imagery analysis challenges US-Iran war claims

Chinese scientists have used detailed satellite imagery analysis to examine damage to US military bases in the Middle East, uncovering discrepancies in both Washington...
title: Chinese data challenges US-Iran war claims; bamboo vs desertification: SCMP’s 7 highlights

author: Albee Zhang
description:
A Type 052D destroyer fired a YJ-20 hypersonic anti-ship missile into the air, Chinese media footage showed, displaying capabilities that pose defence challenges for the United States and its allies.
A YJ-20 missile was launched from a vertical launch system (VLS) of the Type 052D destroyer, according to a video released on Wednesday by state broadcaster CCTV. It is not known when the video was taken.
The YJ-20 missile, also known as a carrier-killer, debuted at Beijing’s large-scale military...
title: What China’s hypersonic anti-ship missile fired from a smaller destroyer signals

author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
China could win the artificial intelligence race if delays in establishing the United States’ AI infrastructure are not addressed, a congressional hearing heard on Thursday, just days before the deadline for the release of new industry guard rails.
“We are in a strategic competition with China to lead the world on AI, and winning that race requires massive capital investment to build the networks that will power tomorrow’s AI applications,” said US Senator Ted Cruz, chairman of the Senate...
title: Will US red tape and other infrastructure delays give China the lead in AI race?

author: William Zheng
description:
The death toll from a landslide in Chongqing province, southwest China, earlier this month rose to 51, with 10 people still missing, local authorities said late on Thursday night.
The landslide, which occurred two weeks ago in Pengshui county, swept away several residential buildings at the foot of a mountain along a riverbank.


Quoting the command centre of the rescue effort, state-run news agency Xinhua said that 51 people had been found and confirmed dead, while 10 were still missing.
Drone...
title: Southwest China landslide death toll rises to 51 as search and rescue continues

author: Haining Gao
description: August 1 sees the 99th anniversary of the founding of the People’s Liberation Army. To mark the occasion, SCMP Plus has republished its February 2026 factsheet on efforts to modernise China’s armed forces.
title: China’s military modernisation

author: Chao Kong
description:
The Pentagon has introduced mandatory testosterone screening for active-duty service members aged 30 and older, with US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth saying the policy is intended to strengthen combat readiness.
Announcing the programme earlier this month, Hegseth said it would help ensure troops remained “strong, resilient and capable”. He argued that the demands of modern warfare required “maximum psychological and mental readiness”.
He also stressed that the initiative had “nothing to do...
title: Will the global testosterone decline accelerate the shift to robot warfare?
